Well-reduced mica, kaṭuphala, kuṣṭha, aśvagandhā, amṛtā, methī, mocarasa, vidārī, muśalī, gokṣūraka, ikṣu, rambhākanda, śatāvarī, ajamodā, māṣa, tila, dhānyaka, yaṣṭī, nāgabalā, balā, madhurikā, jātīphala, and saindhava. RCint 8.236.

One should powder equal parts of bhārṅgī, karkaṭaśṛṅgī, the three pungents (trikaṭu), the two types of cumin (jīradvaya), citraka, the four spices (cāturjāta), punarnavā, gajakaṇā, drākṣā, śaṭhī, vāsaka, the root of śālmali, the three myrobalans (phalatrika), and the seed of the monkey-pomegranate (kapibhava). To this powder, one part of vijayā and two parts of sugar should be added, and the whole should be mixed with honey and ghee. (RCint 8.237)

This pill should be taken by the virtuous at all times, either in a dose of half a *karṣa* or one *karṣa*. It is to be drunk with milk and sugar; it increases virility, provides restraint for lovers, brings women under control, grants supreme pleasure, melts even mature women, nourishes the emaciated, destroys consumption, and eradicates various diseases. (RCint 8.238)
It pacifies cough, dyspnea, and severe diarrhea; it kindles the dull digestive fire; it dispels piles, malabsorption syndrome, urinary disorders, and the masses of phlegm and blood-bile;

it bestows eternal bliss; it brings about the emergence of the play of exceptional poetry and speech; it possesses every virtue; and it is sufficient for great stability in age and for focused meditation. (RC 8.239)
Through practice, Kāmeśvara destroys the decay of old age within a year; he was proclaimed by the venerable Nityanātha as one who brings benefit to all.
Increasing desire even in the elderly during union with mature women, this proven remedy—which has been verified by my own experience—should always be employed by kings.
Equal in measure to the powder of the aphrodisiac group (*vṛṣyagaṇa*), that [powder] is baked in a closed crucible (*puṭapāka*); it is mixed with double the amount of sugar-candy.
This "Jewel Powder" (*cūrṇaratna*) is a supreme aphrodisiac, even beyond the aphrodisiacs, and is a rejuvenative elixir (*rasāyana*). (RCint 8.241)
(Śṛṅgārābhrarasa):
Two palas of pure powdered black mica, one śāṇa each of the other ingredients—
camphor, nutmeg, water, elephant-gallstone (*ibhakaṇā*), tejapatra, and cloves.

Take equal parts of māṃsī, tālīśa, coce, gajakusuma, gada, and dhātakī; then take half a śāṇa each of pathyā, dhātrī, vibhītaka, and trikaṭu, and two śāṇas [of the remaining ingredient]. RCint_8.243 //

One *kola* (120 g) of the substance known as *elā-jātīphala*, purified according to the procedure for the surface of the earth, along with half a *kola* of mercury, should be mixed together and ground with water. Pills should be prepared, each equal in size to a parched, mature chickpea; four of these are to be eaten in the morning, followed by a small amount of fresh ginger with its leaves.

Water drunk at the end certainly and swiftly removes these disorders born of a vitiated digestive fire in the stomach: fever, abdominal diseases, consumption, wasting, cough, dyspnea with swelling, eye afflictions, urinary disorders, disorders of fat, vomiting, colic, acid gastritis, great thirst, and the vast network of abdominal tumors. (RCint 8.245)

This formulation destroys paleness, hemorrhagic fever (raktapitta), diseases born of poison, chronic catarrh, and splenic disorders; it overcomes all diseases arising from undigested matter (āma) and wind, as well as all ailments caused by phlegm and wind. It is strengthening, aphrodisiac, rejuvenating, and highly praised for every disease. Furthermore, it is wholesome when taken with meats, soups, or cow’s milk mixed with clarified butter. (RCint 8.246)

One may joyfully partake of whatever food is desired, served by a charming woman with amorous grace; yet the lover, unsatisfied by the enjoyment of even hundreds of young women, [seeks more]. At first, one should avoid vegetables and sour foods, eating other things according to one’s own will for a few days; through the grace of this [practice], a man becomes long-lived, the very embodiment of desire, and free from wrinkles and grey hair.
(Jayāvaṭī): Equal parts of poison (*viṣa*), the three pungents (*trikaṭuka*), *musta*, turmeric (*haridrā*), neem leaves (*nimbapatraka*),
and *viḍaṅga* as the eighth— this powder, with equal amounts of goat urine, [should be taken].
A pill (vaṭī) should be prepared from chickpeas (caṇaka); jayā is a synergistic agent (yogavāhikā).
(Trinetrarasa):
First, copper treated with sulfur, followed by an equal amount of mercury and sulfur;
this "Three-Eyed" (Trinetra) preparation, ground with clarified butter, possesses a cooling potency and contains half as much sulfur.
If it is hot, one should prepare a medicinal paste (parpaṭī) by grinding it with an equal amount of fragrance;
for this indeed brings about the perfection of the body and destroys all diseases.

Having rubbed pure mercury and twice the amount of sulfur together in a mortar until they form a black collyrium (kajjalī), one should add an equal quantity of magnetic iron (kāntaloha); in its absence, sharp steel (tīkṣṇaka).
O Goddess of the gods, having mixed and ground it with the juices of maidens,
one should then place that pill inside a copper casket for two watches (yāma).
One should cover it with castor leaves and place it upon a heap of grain;
after three days have passed, having extracted it, the flour will become water-soluble.
Kumārī, bhṛṅga, koraṇṭa, kākamācī, punarnavā, nīlī, muṇḍī, nirguṇḍī, sahadevī, and śatāvarī.
Amlaparṇī, gokṣuraka, the root of kacchū, and banyan sprouts—
one should saturate [the powder] with the juices of these, separately seven times each.
When this has dried, one should weigh the powder made from the decoctions of trikaṭu, triphalā, and somarājī; this is the eleventh formulation, consisting of equal parts.
Having combined varā, trikaṭu, agni, viśva, elā, jātīphala,
and lavaṅgaka, one should stir this with honey, crush it, and always consume it.
If one drinks the milk of cows at night, especially that of black cows,
it shall ward off the web of old age, death, and disease for a year.
It is the most excellent for increasing virility and bestows happiness upon hundreds of women;
one's virility does not diminish as long as one does not consume acidic substances.
It is an illuminator, bestowing beauty and always providing nourishment and contentment to those who serve it;
this well-guarded mercury is called Siddhayogeśvara.
(The powder for removing grey hair): Triphalā, iron powder, the root of red citraka, the seed of the fallen small mango tree, palāśa, and small dugdhikā. (RC 8.261)
Having taken these eight [substances] separately, each measuring five palas,
one should mix them together and saturate them with the juice of all the parts of the *palāśa* tree.
One should then take three parts of the seeds of *mahākālaja*,
and having mixed them with one part of black sesame, one should press them together.
That powder should be made into a ball by rubbing it with that oil;
having placed it in a greasy vessel, one should seal it with a shallow bowl.
Having smeared it, one should then place it quickly in a heap of grain;
after a month has passed, having taken it out and worshipped Śiva, the Auspicious One, [one should consume it].
One should consume one *tola* in the morning and one *tola* after a meal.
By practicing this for three months, one undoubtedly destroys gray hair;
by doing so for one year, a person destroys old age and conquers death.

(Regarding the essence of shaking the passion of women: One should grind equal parts of *sugandhaka* mixed with collyrium (*kajjala*) and gold-leaf (*kanaka-bīja*), combined with golden oil (*kanaka-taila*). This is the means for shaking the intoxication of women.
If its pair of stalks, combined with sugar, is consumed, it removes the multitude of urinary disorders;
it provides firmness to the virility, is desirable, and causes the arousal of women during sexual union.
(Regarding the four-faced rasa: Take equal parts of mercury, sulfur, iron, and mica, along with one-fourth part of gold;
having placed everything on a stone slab, rub it with the fresh juice of kanyā.
One should then rub it down with the juices of triphalā, tulasī, and brāhmī,
wrap it in castor leaves, and place it in a heap of grain for three days.
Having prepared it and extracted [the essence], one should combine it with the three myrobalans (*triphalā*) and honey;
this supreme elixir (*rasāyana*) should be administered for all diseases.
For example, one should consume agnibala, which destroys wrinkles and grey hair;
it is nourishing, strengthening, life-prolonging, and brings about the birth of sons. RCint_8.272
Eleven types of consumption (kṣaya), five types of cough (kāsa), eighteen types of leprosy (kuṣṭha), as well as jaundice (pāṇḍuroga) and urinary disorders (prameha); RCint_8.273.
It cures colic, dyspnea, hiccups, weak digestion, and acid bile;
it likewise treats all types of ulcers, āmavāta, erysipelas, and abscesses.
When practiced in succession, it destroys epilepsy, great insanity, all types of hemorrhoids, and skin diseases, just as Indra’s thunderbolt destroys a tree;
this was taught by the four-faced god to Kṛṣṇātreya.
(Gandhalauha) One should consume Gandha-lauha ash mixed with honey and clarified butter for a year with water decocted with the three myrobalans (triphalā).
Thereby, even white hair becomes black, divine vision arises, nourishment and virility are produced, and long life is attained. RCint_8.276.
(Siddhalakṣmīśvararasa):
Having processed mercury six times with gold weighing one-eighth part and with sulfur and orpiment, increasing the quantity of the offering in successive stages,
and placing the fire above and the milk below, O wise ones, place all incomparable accomplishments in your own hands.

(Vahnisiddharasa): Having heated iron, sulphur, and borax together with mercury, and adding more mercury and sulphur to that mixture, it should be ground with the water of a virgin girl and placed in a glass flask. When heated over fire for the sake of perfection, it is "fire-perfected" (vahnisiddha). RCint_8.278.
